# Customizing rulesets: reference

<!-- Generated by `go run ./tools/rulesref` (make ruleset-reference) from definitions/battle_companies/battle_companies.schema.json. Do not edit by hand:
     change the Go model or its descriptions (internal/core/lean/schema_docs_test.go), regenerate the schema, then run `make ruleset-reference`. -->

This page lists every object and key of the Battle Companies file (lean format, `schemaVersion` 2), exactly as the app reads it. It is for
organisers and rules authors who write or edit a ruleset and need to know what a key means, which values it takes and what happens when it is
left out.

It is **generated from the schema**, so it is complete but terse. Where to go instead:

- To learn how to build a ruleset step by step, read the guide: [customizing-rulesets.md](customizing-rulesets.md).
- For how the rules data and the engine fit together, read [definitions.md](definitions.md).

## How to read this page

Each object has a heading, a short description, the places where it appears (`Found at`), an example of its shape and a table of its keys.
The table columns mean:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Key | The name of the key, exactly as written in the file. |
| Type | `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `list of X`, `map of X`, a link to another object, or `any` for a section whose shape the app reads but the checker does not type. |
| Required | `yes` means the key must be present. `no` means it may be left out. |
| Default | What the app uses when the key is absent. `-` means nothing: the key adds nothing when absent. |
| Allowed | The closed vocabulary (`a`, `b`) or the range (`1..50`) the checker enforces. `-` means any value of the type. |
| Description | What the key does. |

A number outside its range, a word outside its vocabulary and a key that is not listed are all errors. An unknown key is never ignored,
except in the objects marked *open*.

The checker (`make check-ruleset`) also verifies what a schema cannot: that names resolve, that charts cover their dice and that parameters
agree with each other. The guide explains its messages.

The examples show the shape of an object with placeholder values, not a recommended setting. Every object lists its required keys; when
there are none, the first keys stand in.

## Document

The whole Battle Companies file: a header, the campaign engine parameters and the sections of rules, items, paths, scenarios, companies and units. The file is complete, not a patch: it is uploaded as the Battle Companies file of a ruleset next to the vanilla file and the glossary. The Go decoder (lean.Decode) is the authority: it also checks names, charts and cross references, which a schema cannot.

The file is one JSON object. Its keys:

Example:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "name": "text",
  "version": "text",
  "campaign": {
    "company": {},
    "recruitment": {},
    "influence": {},
    "progression": {},
    "injuries": {},
    "experience": {},
    "breakPoint": {},
    "rating": {},
    "scenarioSelection": {}
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schemaVersion` | integer | yes | - | `2` | The format version. It must be 2; a file without it, or of another version, is refused with one message. |
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of the ruleset as the admin page and the campaign form list it. |
| `version` | [Scalar](#scalar) | yes | - | - | The version of the ruleset, a string such as "1.1" (a number is read as text). With the name and the short hash it tells two uploads apart. |
| `campaign` | [Campaign](#campaign) | yes | - | - | The engine parameters and tables. |
| `armourUpgrade` | [ArmourUpgrade](#armourupgrade) | no | - | - | The armour upgrade rule. |
| `auras` | [Auras](#auras) | no | - | - | The vocabulary tables of the auras: kinds and groups. |
| `companies` | list of [Company](#company) | no | - | - | The Battle Companies. |
| `creatures` | [Followers](#followers) | no | - | - | The rules of creatures (Baggage Pony, Falcon...). |
| `credit` | any | no | - | - | Who wrote the rules this file transcribes: a list of {name, author, version}. Informational; the app does not read it. |
| `extends` | string | no | - | - | The name of the vanilla file the ruleset is played with, such as "Middle-Earth Strategy Battle Game - 2024". Write it: the upload uses this key to recognise a Battle Companies file (the checker alone does not need it). The file is not merged with anything. |
| `gear` | list of [Gear](#gear) | no | - | - | The items: wargear, equipment, creatures and wanderers, plus annotations of vanilla items. |
| `limits` | list of [Limit](#limit) | no | - | - | The company-wide limits on classes of items or keywords (bows, throwing weapons, Cavalry). |
| `magic` | [Magic](#magic) | no | - | - | Magical powers: casting limits and the range and casting value of each power. |
| `paths` | list of [Path](#path) | no | - | - | The heroic paths. |
| `rules` | list of [Rule](#rule) | no | - | - | The special rules (keywords) that Battle Companies defines or annotates, each defined once and named everywhere else. |
| `scenarios` | list of [Scenario](#scenario) | no | - | - | The scenarios. |
| `units` | list of [Unit](#unit) | no | - | - | Units shared by every company: annotations of vanilla units, or units built on one. |
| `vanilla` | [Vanilla](#vanilla) | no | - | - | What the file says about vanilla things: pins of duplicate names, fill-ins, unsold options. |
| `wanderers` | [Followers](#followers) | no | - | - | The rules of wanderers. |

## Objects

### Campaign

The engine parameters and tables the app switches on: company shape, recruitment, Influence, progression, injuries, experience, the Break Point, rating and scenario selection. A value here replaces the shipped one; the ranges are checked.

Found at: `campaign`.

Example:

```json
{
  "company": {
    "maxModels": 1,
    "leaders": 1,
    "sergeants": 0,
    "heroStart": {},
    "startingInfluence": 0,
    "equipmentSlots": {}
  },
  "recruitment": {
    "die": "text",
    "adjust": {},
    "rare": {}
  },
  "influence": {
    "gains": {}
  },
  "progression": {
    "threshold": 1,
    "warrior": {},
    "hero": {}
  },
  "injuries": {
    "roll": "text"
  },
  "experience": {
    "gains": []
  },
  "breakPoint": {
    "default": {},
    "threshold": {},
    "whenBroken": {}
  },
  "rating": {
    "hero": {}
  },
  "scenarioSelection": {
    "die": "text",
    "tables": []
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `company` | [CompanyRules](#companyrules) | yes | - | - | The shape of a company. |
| `recruitment` | [Recruitment](#recruitment) | yes | - | - | How reinforcements are rolled. |
| `influence` | [Influence](#influence) | yes | - | - | The Influence of the War's Aftermath. |
| `progression` | [Progression](#progression) | yes | - | - | Experience and level-ups. |
| `injuries` | [Injuries](#injuries) | yes | - | - | The injury charts. |
| `experience` | [Experience](#experience) | yes | - | - | The ways to earn Experience. |
| `breakPoint` | [BreakPoint](#breakpoint) | yes | - | - | The Break Point. |
| `rating` | [RatingRules](#ratingrules) | yes | - | - | The rating rules. |
| `scenarioSelection` | [ScenarioSelection](#scenarioselection) | yes | - | - | How a scenario is rolled. |
| `aftermathEffects` | list of [AftermathEffect](#aftermatheffect) | no | - | - | Rewards and bonuses of the War's Aftermath, keyed by the name a scenario reward or an item points at. |
| `againstTheOdds` | [AgainstTheOdds](#againsttheodds) | no | - | - | The Against the Odds bonuses of the lower-rated company, and how the budget and the eligibility work. |
| `characteristicLimits` | [CharacteristicLimits](#characteristiclimits) | no | - | - | The ceilings of the characteristics and the average profile. |
| `gold` | any | no | - | - | How Gold works, in the words of the file. Open data (any JSON, or absent): the app does not read it; Gold is a number on the company, from start.gold and the organiser's grants. |
| `matchInput` | [MatchInput](#matchinput) | no | - | - | What the players enter per match: a description for the people who read the file; the app does not read it. |
| `options` | list of [CampaignOption](#campaignoption) | no | - | - | The campaign options the organiser can switch. The key decides what the app does: an option key the app does not know is listed as unsupported, with a warning in the log. |

### CompanyRules

The shape of a company: its size, officers, the stats of a new hero and the equipment slots.

Found at: `campaign.company`.

Example:

```json
{
  "maxModels": 1,
  "leaders": 1,
  "sergeants": 0,
  "heroStart": {
    "might": 0,
    "will": 0,
    "fate": 0
  },
  "startingInfluence": 0,
  "equipmentSlots": {
    "small": 0,
    "large": 0
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `maxModels` | integer | yes | - | 1..50 | The most models in a company (a company may set its own maxModels). |
| `leaders` | integer | yes | - | 1..3 | How many Leaders a company has. |
| `sergeants` | integer | yes | - | 0..6 | How many Sergeants a company has. Leaders plus sergeants may not exceed maxModels, and the company needs at least one officer. |
| `heroStart` | [HeroGain](#herogain) | yes | - | - | The Might, Will and Fate a new hero starts with. |
| `startingInfluence` | integer | yes | - | 0..100 | The Influence a new company starts with. |
| `equipmentSlots` | [SlotPair](#slotpair) | yes | - | - | The equipment slots of every model before items add any. |
| `oaths` | [Oaths](#oaths) | no | - | - | Fallback oath texts by alignment (good and evil, each {text, vow}) for a company that has no oath of its own. {name} in the text is replaced by the company's name. |

### HeroGain

The Might, Will and Fate a new hero starts with.

Found at: `campaign.company.heroStart`, `companies[].heroes.recruitAsHero`, `paths[].start`.

Example:

```json
{
  "might": 0,
  "will": 0,
  "fate": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `might` | integer | yes | - | 0..5 | Might points. |
| `will` | integer | yes | - | 0..5 | Will points. |
| `fate` | integer | yes | - | 0..5 | Fate points. |

### SlotPair

A number of small and of large equipment slots.

Found at: `campaign.company.equipmentSlots`.

Example:

```json
{
  "small": 0,
  "large": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `small` | integer | yes | - | 0..10 | Small slots. |
| `large` | integer | yes | - | 0..10 | Large slots. |

### Oaths

The fallback oaths of the companies that have none of their own, one per alignment.

Found at: `campaign.company.oaths`.

Example:

```json
{
  "evil": {
    "text": "text",
    "vow": "text"
  },
  "good": {
    "text": "text",
    "vow": "text"
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evil` | [Oath](#oath) | no | - | - | The oath of an evil company. |
| `good` | [Oath](#oath) | no | - | - | The oath of a good company. |

### Oath

The oath the player swears when taking command of the company.

Found at: `campaign.company.oaths.evil`, `campaign.company.oaths.good`, `companies[].oath`.

Example:

```json
{
  "text": "text",
  "vow": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The oath. {name} stands exactly once, not at the start or the end, where the company's name goes. |
| `vow` | string | no | - | - | The label of the button the player presses (1 to 40 characters). |

### Recruitment

How reinforcements are rolled: the die, how Influence moves the die, and which models count towards a Rare limit.

Found at: `campaign.recruitment`.

Example:

```json
{
  "die": "text",
  "adjust": {
    "maxPerAttempt": 0,
    "direction": "up",
    "costPerPoint": 0
  },
  "rare": {
    "injuredCount": true,
    "deadCount": true,
    "promotedCount": true
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `die` | [DiceSpec](#dicespec) | yes | - | - | The recruiting die: one die, written dN. Every reinforcement and special chart must cover 1..N exactly once. |
| `adjust` | [Adjust](#adjust) | yes | - | - | How Influence moves the die. |
| `rare` | [RareRule](#rarerule) | yes | - | - | Which models count towards a Rare N limit. |

### Adjust

How a player may spend Influence to move the recruiting die.

Found at: `campaign.recruitment.adjust`.

Example:

```json
{
  "maxPerAttempt": 0,
  "direction": "up",
  "costPerPoint": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `maxPerAttempt` | integer | yes | - | 0..20 | The most points the die may be moved in one recruiting attempt, over both charts together. |
| `direction` | string | yes | - | `up`, `down`, `both` | up, down or both: the direction the die may be moved. |
| `costPerPoint` | integer | yes | - | 0..10 | The Influence one point of movement costs. |

### RareRule

Which models of a profile count towards its Rare N limit.

Found at: `campaign.recruitment.rare`.

Example:

```json
{
  "injuredCount": true,
  "deadCount": true,
  "promotedCount": true
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `injuredCount` | boolean | yes | - | - | true: an injured model counts towards Rare N. |
| `deadCount` | boolean | yes | - | - | true: a dead model counts towards Rare N. |
| `promotedCount` | boolean | yes | - | - | true: a model that was promoted to another profile still counts for its old profile. |

### Influence

The Influence a company earns after a match.

Found at: `campaign.influence`.

Example:

```json
{
  "gains": {
    "participating": 0,
    "draw": 0,
    "win": 0
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gains` | [InfluenceGains](#influencegains) | yes | - | - | The Influence earned after a match. |
| `spend` | any | no | - | - | What Influence buys, as free player-facing prose and data (a list of {key, name, text, ...}). Genuinely open: the app does not read or print it. |

### InfluenceGains

The Influence of the War's Aftermath.

Found at: `campaign.influence.gains`.

Example:

```json
{
  "participating": 0,
  "draw": 0,
  "win": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `participating` | integer | yes | - | 0..20 | Influence for taking part in a match. |
| `draw` | integer | yes | - | 0..20 | Influence for a draw. |
| `win` | integer | yes | - | 0..20 | Influence for a win. |

### Progression

Experience, level-ups and the dice of the warrior and hero progression.

Found at: `campaign.progression`.

Example:

```json
{
  "threshold": 1,
  "warrior": {
    "roll": "text",
    "noPromotion": {}
  },
  "hero": {
    "roll": "text",
    "rollsPerProgression": 1,
    "choose": 1
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `threshold` | integer | yes | - | 1..50 | Experience Points per level-up: a model rolls floor(XP / threshold) times and nothing is spent. |
| `warrior` | [WarriorProgress](#warriorprogress) | yes | - | - | The warrior progression. |
| `hero` | [HeroProgress](#heroprogress) | yes | - | - | The hero progression. |

### WarriorProgress

The warrior progression: the die, its table and what a warrior with no promotion gains.

Found at: `campaign.progression.warrior`.

Example:

```json
{
  "roll": "text",
  "noPromotion": {
    "courage": 0,
    "intelligence": 0,
    "maximum": 1
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roll` | [DiceSpec](#dicespec) | yes | - | - | The die of the warrior table; its rows must cover it exactly once. |
| `noPromotion` | [NoPromotion](#nopromotion) | yes | - | - | What a warrior with no promotion gains. |
| `table` | list of [TableRow](#tablerow) | no | - | - | The rows of the warrior table. Keys noChange, promoted and heroInTheMaking are the ones the engine knows. |

### NoPromotion

What a warrior whose promotion roll finds no promotion gains instead.

Found at: `campaign.progression.warrior.noPromotion`.

Example:

```json
{
  "courage": 0,
  "intelligence": 0,
  "maximum": 1
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `courage` | integer | yes | - | 0..5 | The Courage improvement (a lower Courage number is better). |
| `intelligence` | integer | yes | - | 0..5 | The Intelligence improvement. |
| `maximum` | integer | yes | - | 1..10 | The best value (as a number, 3 for 3+) the improvement may reach. |

### TableRow

A row of the warrior progression table.

Found at: `campaign.progression.warrior.table[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "roll": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roll` | [Roll](#roll) | yes | - | - | The roll or range the row covers. |
| `key` | string | no | - | - | The key the engine switches on. |
| `name` | string | no | - | - | The name of the result. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule text of the result. |

### HeroProgress

The hero progression: the dice rolled and how many results the player keeps.

Found at: `campaign.progression.hero`.

Example:

```json
{
  "roll": "text",
  "rollsPerProgression": 1,
  "choose": 1
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roll` | [DiceSpec](#dicespec) | yes | - | - | The die of a path table (a path may name its own). |
| `rollsPerProgression` | integer | yes | - | 1..6 | How many results are rolled for one level-up. |
| `choose` | integer | yes | - | 1..6 | How many of the rolled results the player keeps; at most rollsPerProgression. |

### Injuries

The injury charts, the die they are rolled on and the treatments. The chart rows and the treatments are read by the engine; the prose keys (applies, deathOfAHero, healing, retirement, rollModifier) are rule text for the players.

Found at: `campaign.injuries`.

Example:

```json
{
  "roll": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roll` | [DiceSpec](#dicespec) | yes | - | - | The injury die, such as 2d6. Both charts must cover its totals exactly once. |
| `applies` | string | no | - | - | Who rolls on the charts. Prose shown to the players. |
| `deathOfAHero` | string | no | - | - | What happens when a Leader is slain. Prose shown to the players. |
| `healing` | [InjuryHealingText](#injuryhealingtext) | no | - | - | How injuries are healed. Prose shown to the players. |
| `hero` | list of [InjuryRow](#injuryrow) | no | - | - | The hero injury chart. |
| `retirement` | [InjuryRetirement](#injuryretirement) | no | - | - | Forced retirement. Prose; the count is the row's retireAtCount. |
| `rollModifier` | [InjuryRollModifier](#injuryrollmodifier) | no | - | - | Modifiers of the injury roll. Prose; the modifier is a campaign.aftermathEffects entry. |
| `treatment` | [InjuryTreatment](#injurytreatment) | no | - | - | How Influence treats injuries. |
| `warrior` | list of [InjuryRow](#injuryrow) | no | - | - | The warrior injury chart. |

### InjuryHealingText

The rulebook text of how injuries are healed. Prose; the app does not read it.

Found at: `campaign.injuries.healing`.

Example:

```json
{
  "hero": "text",
  "warrior": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` | string | no | - | - | How a hero is healed. |
| `warrior` | string | no | - | - | How a warrior is healed. |

### InjuryRow

A row of an injury chart. The engine reads effects (remove, missNextGame, fullRecovery) to decide what the result does, and persistent, retireAtCount, statChanges, disables and grantsAtCount for a hero's lasting injuries.

Found at: `campaign.injuries.hero[]`, `campaign.injuries.warrior[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "roll": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roll` | [Roll](#roll) | yes | - | - | The roll or range the row covers. |
| `cancelsMissedGame` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the result cancels the missed next game. |
| `clearsAfterGames` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | The injury ends after this many games. |
| `disables` | list of [InjuryDisable](#injurydisable) | no | - | - | What a lasting injury takes from the hero. |
| `effects` | list of string | no | - | `remove`, `missNextGame`, `fullRecovery`, `healOneInjury`, `reduceMovement`, `noShield`, `noTwoHandedWeapon`, `noPike`, `noBow`, `noStandFast`, `noHeroicActionsOnCompany` | What the result does. remove (the model dies), missNextGame and fullRecovery decide the result; the others (healOneInjury, reduceMovement, noShield...) label the effect for the reader and are done by the other keys of the row. |
| `experience` | [DiceSpec](#dicespec) | no | - | - | The die of grantsExperience in the rulebook's words (D3). The app reads grantsExperience. |
| `grantsAtCount` | map of [CountGrant](#countgrant) | no | - | - | Special rules the hero gets from a count of the injury on: {"2": {specialRule}}. |
| `grantsExperience` | [DiceGrant](#dicegrant) | no | - | - | Experience rolled on a die when the result comes up. |
| `grantsInfluence` | [DiceGrant](#dicegrant) | no | - | - | Influence rolled on a die for the company when the result comes up. |
| `healable` | boolean | no | - | - | true: a treatment can remove the injury. |
| `healableBy` | list of string | no | - | at least 1 items | The treatment methods that can remove the injury (a key of campaign.injuries.treatment.hero), for a status such as T'is Just a Scratch. |
| `heals` | [InjuryHeals](#injuryheals) | no | - | - | The injuries a healing result removes. |
| `influence` | [DiceSpec](#dicespec) | no | - | - | The die of grantsInfluence in the rulebook's words (D6). The app reads grantsInfluence. |
| `key` | string | no | - | - | The key the engine switches on (dead, injured, fullRecovery...). A row with no effects is read by its key: dead, injured, else a full recovery. |
| `name` | string | no | - | - | The name of the result. |
| `optionalReroll` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the player may roll again on the chart instead of taking the result (T'is Just a Scratch). |
| `persistent` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the hero keeps the injury and counts how often it suffered it (arm wound, leg wound, broken honour). |
| `reroll` | [InjuryReroll](#injuryreroll) | no | - | - | How the re-roll of an optionalReroll result works. |
| `retireAtCount` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | A persistent injury forces the hero to retire at this count, as the Dead result. |
| `stat` | map of integer | no | - | - | The characteristics changed, as {characteristic: change}, for the reader of the file. The app reads statChanges. |
| `statChanges` | list of [InjuryChange](#injurychange) | no | - | - | The characteristics the result changes (a gain on a row that is not a persistent injury, a loss on one). |
| `stat_note` | string | no | - | - | A note on stat, for the reader of the file. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule text of the result. |

### InjuryDisable

What a lasting injury takes from a hero: the benefit of gear of some classes or by name, or an ability.

Found at: `campaign.injuries.hero[].disables[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "kind": "gearClass"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | yes | - | `gearClass`, `gearItem`, `ability` | gearClass (items of the listed classes give no benefit), gearItem (the named items give none) or ability (the hero loses the ability). |
| `classes` | list of string | no | - | `melee`, `spear`, `two_handed`, `mount`, `bow`, `armour`, `throwing`, `shield`, `instrument`, `consumable`, `lance`, `banner`, `missile`, `crossbow`, `other` | The gear classes, for kind gearClass. |
| `key` | string | no | - | `standFast`, `heroicActionsOnCompany` | The ability, for kind ability: standFast or heroicActionsOnCompany. |
| `names` | list of string | no | - | at least 1 items | The item names, for kind gearItem. |

### InjuryChange

A characteristic an injury changes: a gain on a row that is not a persistent injury, a loss (per count) on one.

Found at: `campaign.injuries.hero[].statChanges[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "stat": "movement",
  "amount": -20
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stat` | string | yes | - | `movement`, `fight`, `shoot`, `strength`, `defence`, `attack`, `wounds`, `courage`, `intelligence`, `might`, `will`, `fate` | The characteristic changed. |
| `amount` | integer | yes | - | -20..20 | The change, a positive gain or a negative loss. |
| `capAtPathMaximum` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the gain stops at the maximum of the hero's path. Informational; the app does not read it. |
| `minimum` | integer or null | no | - | 0..20 | The lowest value the characteristic may reach; null for no floor. Informational; the app does not read it. |
| `per` | string | no | - | `count` | count: the amount is applied once per time the hero has the injury. |
| `permanent` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the change stays for good. Informational; a row that is not persistent always keeps its gain. |
| `raisesPathMaximum` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the gain also raises the path's maximum. Informational; the app does not read it. |

| `includesRerolls` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the modifier also applies to a re-roll. |
| `replacedBy` | string | no | - | - | Where the modifier is defined, for the reader of the file. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule in words. |

| `warrior` | [WarriorTreatment](#warriortreatment) | no | - | - | The warrior treatment. |

### HeroTreatment

| `who` | string | no | - | `modelsOnTheHill`, `defenderWithin6OfTheGate`, `defenderBaggagePonies`, `neutralModels`, `ownModelsNotArrived` | Who it concerns: modelsOnTheHill, defenderWithin6OfTheGate, defenderBaggagePonies, neutralModels or ownModelsNotArrived. |

### AftermathEffect

A reward or bonus of the War's Aftermath: a scenario reward (kind influence, experience or freeEquipment), a consumable item (injuryRollModifier, injuryRollReplacement), a die modifier (rendezvous and vantagePoint, by key) or the effect of an Against the Odds bonus. The kind and the keys the engine acts on are listed first; the others state the rule in data for the reader of the file.

Found at: `campaign.aftermathEffects[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "key": "text",
  "kind": "rerolls"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | - | not empty | The key a scenario reward (rewards[].effect) or an item (aftermathEffect) points at; unique. rendezvous and vantagePoint also need a range. |
| `kind` | string | yes | - | `rerolls`, `influence`, `experiencePerModel`, `injuryRollModifier`, `injuryRollReplacement`, `reinforcementRollModifier`, `freeEquipment`, `experience`, `scenarioTableModifier`, `magicalPower` | What the effect is. influence and experience pay a scenario reward (amount); freeEquipment lets a model take an item worth at most maxInfluenceValue; injuryRollModifier and injuryRollReplacement are consumables; reinforcementRollModifier and scenarioTableModifier move a die (rendezvous, vantagePoint); rerolls, experiencePerModel and magicalPower are rules the players apply. |
| `activatedBy` | [ActivatedBy](#activatedby) | no | - | - | Who may use a consumable and when. |
| `amount` | integer | no | - | 0..100 | The Influence or Experience Points a reward gives (kind influence or experience). |
| `applies` | string | no | - | `eachInjuryRoll` | eachInjuryRoll: the modifier applies to every injury roll of the company. |
| `choice` | string | no | - | `player` | player: the player decides whether to use it. |
| `clamp` | list of integer | no | - | 0..100; 2..2 items | [low, high]: the modified injury total is held to this range. |
| `consumes` | string | no | - | `oneItem`, `thisItem` | oneItem or thisItem: what is used up when the effect is used. |
| `count` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | How many re-rolls (kind rerolls). |
| `die` | string | no | - | `second` | second: the modifier moves the second die of the scenario table. Informational. |
| `gains` | [ATOReward](#atoreward) | no | - | - | The Influence or Experience by result of an Against the Odds bonus: win for a Victory, other for a Draw or Defeat. |
| `ignoresWill` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the power works even when the model has no Will left. Informational. |
| `includesHealOneInjury` | boolean | no | - | - | true: a Full Recovery from the effect also heals one injury. Informational. |
| `includesHeroReroll` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the modifier also applies to a hero's re-roll. Informational. |
| `maxInfluenceValue` | integer | no | - | 0..100 | freeEquipment: the most Influence the free item may cost. |
| `modifier` | integer | no | - | -12..12 | injuryRollModifier: added to the injury total. |
| `noRoll` | boolean | no | - | - | injuryRollReplacement: true means the model does not roll on the chart. |
| `power` | string | no | - | not empty | magicalPower: the power granted. |
| `range` | list of integer | no | - | -6..6; 2..2 items | [low, high], how far the effect moves a die; -6..6. |
| `result` | string | no | - | not empty | injuryRollReplacement: the key of the injury result the model counts as having rolled; required for that kind. |
| `rolls` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | How many rolls the die modifier applies to. |
| `scenario` | string | no | - | not empty | The scenario the effect belongs to, as named in scenarios[]. |
| `source` | string | no | - | - | Where the rule comes from in the rulebook, for the reader of the file. |
| `stackable` | boolean | no | - | - | false: only one of the effect counts per aftermath. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule in words, shown to the players. |
| `to` | string | no | - | `leader` | leader: the reward goes to the Leader. |
| `usableIn` | list of string | no | - | `game`, `warsAftermath` | Where a re-roll may be used: game or warsAftermath. |
| `usesPerAftermath` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | How often the effect may be used in one aftermath. Informational. |
| `when` | string | no | - | `beforeInjuryRolls`, `firstReinforcementRollThisAftermath`, `nextScenarioTableRoll`, `nextGame` | When a perk or consumable is used: beforeInjuryRolls, firstReinforcementRollThisAftermath, nextScenarioTableRoll or nextGame. |
| `who` | string | no | - | not empty | Who gets the effect, in words of the data (victor, lowerRatedCompany ...). Open: the app does not read it. |

### ActivatedBy

Who may use a consumable item and when.

Found at: `campaign.aftermathEffects[].activatedBy`.

Example:

```json
{
  "carrier": "hero",
  "fledModelIs": "notCasualty",
  "requires": [
    "participated"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `carrier` | string | no | - | `hero`, `anyModel` | hero: only a hero may use it; anyModel: any model. |
| `fledModelIs` | string | no | - | `notCasualty` | notCasualty: a model that fled the board is not a casualty. Informational. |
| `requires` | list of string | no | - | `participated`, `casualty`, `notCasualty` | What must hold: participated (the model took part), casualty, notCasualty. |

### ATOReward

A reward by result.

Found at: `campaign.aftermathEffects[].gains`, `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[].gains.experiencePerModel`, `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[].gains.influence`.

Example:

```json
{
  "win": 0,
  "other": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `win` | integer | yes | - | 0..20 | The reward for a Victory. |
| `other` | integer | yes | - | 0..20 | The reward for a Draw or a Defeat. |

### AgainstTheOdds

The bonuses the lower rated company may take after the scenario roll, and the rules of the budget and of who may choose. The bonuses and the budget are read by the engine; the other keys are rule text.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds`.

Example:

```json
{
  "bonuses": [
    {
      "key": "text",
      "name": "text",
      "rating": 0
    }
  ],
  "budget": {
    "inclusive": true,
    "rule": "ratingAfterBonusesNotAboveOpponent",
    "text": "text"
  },
  "eligible": {
    "company": "lowerRating",
    "compare": "strictlyLower",
    "ratingBeforeBonuses": true
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bonuses` | list of [ATOBonus](#atobonus) | no | - | - | The bonuses, in the order the players see them. |
| `budget` | [ATOBudget](#atobudget) | no | - | - | The Rating budget of the bonuses. |
| `eligible` | [ATOEligible](#atoeligible) | no | - | - | Who may choose bonuses. |
| `selectedAt` | string | no | - | `afterScenarioRollBeforeSetup` | When the bonuses are chosen: afterScenarioRollBeforeSetup. Informational. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule in words. Shown to the players. |

### ATOBonus

One Against the Odds bonus. influence, experience and reroll are plain switches (gains, count); toolKit (kits, purchase), wanderer and ambush are bonuses the app has its own windows for. Any other key is a plain bonus that costs its rating and adds its gains.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "key": "text",
  "name": "text",
  "rating": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | - | not empty | The key of the bonus; unique. influence, experience, reroll, toolKit, wanderer and ambush have their own behaviour. |
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name the players see. |
| `rating` | integer | yes | - | 0..1000 | The Rating the bonus adds to the company's rating (for the Tool Kit, per kit). |
| `affects` | string | no | - | `singleDieOrSingleResult` | What a re-roll may re-roll: singleDieOrSingleResult. Informational. |
| `appliesIn` | list of string | no | - | `setup`, `game`, `aftermath`, `scenarioChoice` | When the bonus acts: setup, game, aftermath or scenarioChoice. A practice match refuses the bonuses that only pay in the aftermath. |
| `carriesOver` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the bonus lasts beyond the match. Informational. |
| `count` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | How many re-rolls the bonus gives (reroll). |
| `expires` | string | no | - | `endOfMatchAftermath`, `endOfMatch` | When the bonus ends. Informational. |
| `gains` | [ATOGains](#atogains) | no | - | - | What the bonus adds after the match. |
| `grants` | [ATOGrant](#atogrant) | no | - | - | What a structured bonus gives. |
| `kits` | list of [ATOKit](#atokit) | no | - | - | The kits of the Tool Kit bonus. |
| `purchase` | [ATOPurchase](#atopurchase) | no | - | - | How many kits may be bought (Tool Kit). |
| `temporary` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the bonus lasts for one match (wanderer). Informational. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule in words. |
| `usableIn` | list of string | no | - | `game`, `warsAftermath` | Where a re-roll may be used: game or warsAftermath. Informational. |

### ATOGains

The rewards a bonus adds after the match.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[].gains`.

Example:

```json
{
  "experiencePerModel": {
    "win": 0,
    "other": 0
  },
  "influence": {
    "win": 0,
    "other": 0
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `experiencePerModel` | [ATOReward](#atoreward) | no | - | - | Experience added for every model of the company, by result. |
| `influence` | [ATOReward](#atoreward) | no | - | - | Influence added for the company, by result. |

### ATOGrant

What a structured bonus gives: loaned equipment (Tool Kit), a temporary model (Wanderer) or the choice of the scenario (Ambush!). The app reads these bonuses by their key; these keys state the rules in data for the reader of the file and are not read.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[].grants`.

Example:

```json
{
  "addsRating": true,
  "assignAt": "beforeSetup",
  "assignTo": "anyModelOfTheMatch"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `addsRating` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the loaned items add to the Rating. |
| `assignAt` | string | no | - | `beforeSetup` | When the items are handed out: beforeSetup. |
| `assignTo` | string | no | - | `anyModelOfTheMatch` | Who gets them: anyModelOfTheMatch. |
| `carriesOver` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the grant lasts beyond the match. |
| `chosenBy` | string | no | - | `lowerRatedCompany` | Who chooses the scenario: lowerRatedCompany. |
| `count` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | How many models the grant adds. |
| `countsTowardsBreakPoint` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the temporary model counts for the Break Point. |
| `countsTowardsMaxModels` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the temporary model counts towards the company's size. |
| `duration` | string | no | - | `thisMatch` | How long the choice holds: thisMatch. |
| `exclusiveWithPermanentWanderer` | boolean | no | - | - | true: a company with a permanent Wanderer cannot take it. |
| `expires` | string | no | - | `endOfMatchAftermath`, `endOfMatch` | When the grant ends. |
| `from` | string | no | - | not empty | Where the choice comes from (data.wanderers.items, scenarios). |
| `gainsExperience` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the temporary model earns Experience. |
| `goldCost` | integer | no | - | 0..1000 | The Gold it costs. |
| `ignores` | list of string | no | - | `capacity`, `alignment` | The rules the loaned items ignore: capacity, alignment. |
| `influenceCost` | integer | no | - | 0..1000 | The Influence it costs. |
| `kind` | string | no | - | `loanedEquipment`, `temporaryModel`, `chooseScenario` | loanedEquipment, temporaryModel or chooseScenario. |
| `oncePerKit` | boolean | no | - | - | true: one of each kit. |
| `persistsAfterMatch` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the model stays after the match. |
| `ratingCost` | string | no | - | `bonusRating` | bonusRating: it costs the bonus's rating. |
| `replaces` | string | no | - | `scenarioTableRoll` | What the choice replaces: scenarioTableRoll. |
| `rolesBy` | string | no | - | `scenarioRules` | How the roles are given: scenarioRules. |
| `rollsInjuries` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the temporary model rolls on the injury chart. |
| `rules` | string | no | - | - | The rules of the temporary model in words. |
| `stillApplies` | list of string | no | - | `heroOnly` | The restrictions that still apply: heroOnly. |
| `takesRosterSlot` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the temporary model takes a place of the roster. |
| `usableByTemporaryWanderer` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the temporary Wanderer may use the items. |

### ATOKit

A kit of the Tool Kit bonus: the items it lends.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[].kits[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "text",
  "items": [
    {
      "equipment": "text"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of the kit; the app makes the key of the kit from its first word (Healer's Kit is healer). Unique. |
| `items` | list of [ATOKitItem](#atokititem) | yes | - | at least 1 items | The items the kit lends. |

### ATOKitItem

An item of a kit and how many copies the kit holds.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[].kits[].items[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "equipment": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `equipment` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of an equipment item of the file; a name with (X) asks the player for the weapon it is on. |
| `count` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | How many copies the kit holds; default 1. |

### ATOPurchase

How many kits the Tool Kit bonus may be bought for.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[].purchase`.

Example:

```json
{
  "chooses": "oneKit",
  "distinctKits": true,
  "maxPurchases": 1
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chooses` | string | no | - | `oneKit` | oneKit: each purchase is one kit. |
| `distinctKits` | boolean | no | - | - | true: a kit may be bought once. Informational; the app always refuses a kit twice. |
| `maxPurchases` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | The most kits that may be bought. |
| `ratingPerKit` | boolean | no | - | - | true: every kit costs the bonus's rating. Informational; the Tool Kit always does. |

### ATOBudget

The rule that the sum of the Ratings of the chosen bonuses may not take the lower company above its opponent's Rating.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.budget`.

Example:

```json
{
  "inclusive": true,
  "rule": "ratingAfterBonusesNotAboveOpponent",
  "text": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inclusive` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the bonuses may take the lower company exactly up to its opponent's Rating ("must not exceed"); false: they must leave it below. |
| `rule` | string | no | - | `ratingAfterBonusesNotAboveOpponent` | ratingAfterBonusesNotAboveOpponent. Informational. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule in words. |

### ATOEligible

Who may choose bonuses: the company with the strictly lower Rating, compared before the bonuses.

Found at: `campaign.againstTheOdds.eligible`.

Example:

```json
{
  "company": "lowerRating",
  "compare": "strictlyLower",
  "ratingBeforeBonuses": true
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `company` | string | no | - | `lowerRating` | lowerRating: the company that chooses. Informational. |
| `compare` | string | no | - | `strictlyLower` | strictlyLower: at equal Ratings nobody chooses. Informational. |
| `ratingBeforeBonuses` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the comparison is made before the bonuses. Informational. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule in words. |

### CharacteristicLimits

The ceilings of the characteristics: which ones improve downwards, the highest each one goes, the average profile the hero rating starts from, and the cap on the total improvement of Courage and Intelligence.

Found at: `campaign.characteristicLimits`.

Example:

```json
{
  "average": {},
  "increases": {
    "courageIntelligenceTotalCap": {}
  },
  "lowerIsBetter": [
    "movement"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `average` | map of integer | no | - | - | The average value of each characteristic of a profile ({attack: 1, courage: 7 ...}); the base the hero rating counts points above. A characteristic that is absent is not counted. |
| `increases` | [CharacteristicIncrease](#characteristicincrease) | no | - | - | Limits on the improvements a hero adds up. |
| `lowerIsBetter` | list of string | no | - | `movement`, `fight`, `shoot`, `strength`, `defence`, `attack`, `wounds`, `courage`, `intelligence`, `might`, `will`, `fate` | The characteristics where a lower number is better (Shoot, Courage, Intelligence): an improvement lowers them and best, not max, is their limit. |
| `peak` | [PeakLimits](#peaklimits) | no | - | - | The highest each characteristic goes, whatever the path. |

### CharacteristicIncrease

Limits on the improvements a hero adds up.

Found at: `campaign.characteristicLimits.increases`.

Example:

```json
{
  "courageIntelligenceTotalCap": {
    "value": 1
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `courageIntelligenceTotalCap` | [TotalCap](#totalcap) | no | - | - | The cap on the total improvement of Courage and Intelligence. |

### TotalCap

The most Courage and Intelligence may be improved in total from the unmodified profile.

Found at: `campaign.characteristicLimits.increases.courageIntelligenceTotalCap`.

Example:

```json
{
  "value": 1
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | integer | yes | - | 1..10 | The most points, 1..10, Courage and Intelligence may be improved in total. |
| `includesGear` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the improvement from gear counts in the total. |

### PeakLimits

The overall limit of each characteristic (one key per characteristic, only those that have one), and the Will maximum some paths have of their own.

Found at: `campaign.characteristicLimits.peak`.

Example:

```json
{
  "attack": {
    "best": 1,
    "max": 1,
    "maxIncrease": 0
  },
  "courage": {
    "best": 1,
    "max": 1,
    "maxIncrease": 0
  },
  "defence": {
    "best": 1,
    "max": 1,
    "maxIncrease": 0
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attack` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Attacks. |
| `courage` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Courage. |
| `defence` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Defence. |
| `fate` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Fate. |
| `fight` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Fight. |
| `intelligence` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Intelligence. |
| `might` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Might. |
| `movement` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Movement. |
| `shoot` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Shoot. |
| `strength` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Strength. |
| `will` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Will. |
| `willMaxOverrides` | map of integer | no | - | - | The Will maximum a path has of its own, by path name (1..10); it replaces the peak's Will maximum for heroes of that path. |
| `wounds` | [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The limit of Wounds. |

### StatLimit

How far one characteristic may be improved. A key that is absent sets no limit of that kind. The same shape is used by the overall peak and by a path's maximums.

Found at: `campaign.characteristicLimits.peak.attack`, `campaign.characteristicLimits.peak.courage`, `campaign.characteristicLimits.peak.defence`.

Example:

```json
{
  "best": 1,
  "max": 1,
  "maxIncrease": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `best` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | The best (lowest) value of a characteristic where lower is better. |
| `max` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | The highest value of a characteristic where higher is better. |
| `maxIncrease` | integer | no | - | 0..20 | The most points level-ups may add to the profile (without gear). |

### MatchInput

What the players enter per match, described for the people who read the file. The app builds its match forms from its own tables (the experience gains, the scenarios, Against the Odds) and does not read this description.

Found at: `campaign.matchInput`.

Example:

```json
{
  "aftermath": {
    "order": [],
    "rewards": "text"
  },
  "gold": {
    "scenarioRewards": true,
    "text": "text"
  },
  "perCompany": [
    {
      "key": "text"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aftermath` | [MatchAftermath](#matchaftermath) | no | - | - | How the aftermath is applied. |
| `gold` | [MatchGold](#matchgold) | no | - | - | What the rulebook says about Gold in a scenario. |
| `perCompany` | list of [InputField](#inputfield) | no | - | - | What is entered for each company. |
| `perModel` | list of [InputField](#inputfield) | no | - | - | What is entered for each model. |
| `result` | [MatchResult](#matchresult) | no | - | - | How the winner is decided. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | What the players enter, in words. |

### MatchAftermath

The order in which the War's Aftermath is applied.

```json
{
  "order": [
    "injuries"
  ],
  "rewards": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | list of string | no | - | `injuries`, `experience`, `progression`, `influence` | The steps of the aftermath, in order: injuries, experience, progression, influence. |
| `rewards` | string | no | - | - | Where the scenario rewards come from and when they apply. |

### MatchGold

What the rulebook says about Gold in a scenario.

Found at: `campaign.matchInput.gold`.

Example:

```json
{
  "scenarioRewards": true,
  "text": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scenarioRewards` | boolean | no | - | - | true: scenarios reward Gold. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rule in words. |

### InputField

One thing the players enter, per company or per model.

Found at: `campaign.matchInput.perCompany[]`, `campaign.matchInput.perModel[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "key": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | - | not empty | The key of the field; unique in its list. |
| `computed` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the app works it out; nobody enters it. |
| `computedFrom` | string | no | - | - | What it is worked out from. |
| `declaredBy` | string | no | - | `opponent` | opponent: the other player says. |
| `default` | any | no | - | - | The starting value: true or false for a flag, a number for a count, the chosen word for an enum. Open data. |
| `experience` | string | no | - | - | The key of the experience gain (campaign.experience.gains) it records. |
| `feeds` | list of string | no | - | `influence`, `experience`, `rerolls`, `rewards`, `itemUse`, `breakPoint`, `injuries` | What the field feeds: influence, experience, rerolls, rewards, itemUse, breakPoint, injuries. |
| `from` | string | no | - | - | Where the entries come from. |
| `inferred` | list of string | no | - | - | What follows from the field, for the reader of the file. |
| `maxPerCompany` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | The most models of one company that can have it. |
| `min` | integer | no | - | 0..100 | The lowest number that can be entered. |
| `optional` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the field may stay empty. |
| `options` | any | no | - | - | The words to choose from, as a list, or the path of the table they come from. Open data. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | What the players enter, in words. |
| `type` | string | no | - | `enum`, `multiSelect`, `select`, `integer`, `count`, `flag`, `flags`, `scoringObjectives` | How it is entered: enum or select (one of the options), multiSelect (several), integer, count, flag (yes or no), flags, scoringObjectives. |
| `when` | string | no | - | - | When the field is asked for. |
| `who` | string | no | - | - | Who it concerns. |

### MatchResult

How the winner of a match is decided.

Found at: `campaign.matchInput.result`.

Example:

```json
{
  "decidedBy": "victoryPoints",
  "outcomes": [
    "win"
  ],
  "tie": "draw"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decidedBy` | string | no | - | `victoryPoints` | victoryPoints: the company with the most Victory Points wins. |
| `outcomes` | list of string | no | - | `win`, `draw`, `loss` | The results a match can have: win, draw, loss. |
| `tie` | string | no | - | `draw` | What equal Victory Points are: draw. |

### CampaignOption

A setting the file offers the organiser of a campaign: a rule variant (scope rules) or how the app behaves (scope app). The app switches the options it knows by key and lists any other as unsupported.

Found at: `campaign.options[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "key": "text",
  "scope": "rules",
  "label": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | - | not empty | The key of the option; unique. The keys the app knows are heroesDropProfileGear, customOnTheirOwnPath, shakeTheTable and manualRolls. |
| `scope` | string | yes | - | `rules`, `app` | rules: a rule variant that changes the game; app: how the app behaves. |
| `label` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name the campaign form shows. |
| `default` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the option is on in a new campaign. |
| `description` | string | no | - | - | A sentence shown under the label. |
| `implemented` | boolean or null | no | - | - | false: the file lists the option but the app cannot switch it on. Absent means implemented, if the app knows the key. |
| `swaps` | [OptionSwap](#optionswap) | no | - | - | For an option that puts one path in the place of another. |

### OptionSwap

The path an option puts in the place of another path (a house rule that swaps one path for another).

Found at: `campaign.options[].swaps`.

Example:

```json
{
  "path": "text",
  "replaces": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | - | not empty | The path used instead. |
| `replaces` | string | yes | - | not empty | The path (or rule) it replaces. |

### ArmourUpgrade

The rule "Upgrade Armour by one stage": the names of each stage, lowest first, and what an upgrade costs.

Found at: `armourUpgrade`.

Example:

```json
{
  "stages": [
    [
      "text"
    ]
  ],
  "influence": 0,
  "rating": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stages` | list of list of string | yes | - | - | The names of each stage, lowest first; a list of lists of equivalent names. |
| `influence` | integer | yes | - | 0..100 | The Influence one upgrade costs. |
| `rating` | [Rating](#rating) | yes | - | - | The rating one upgrade adds. |
| `gold` | [Rating](#rating) | no | - | - | The Gold one upgrade costs; default the rating. |

### Auras

The aura vocabulary tables: kinds and groups, once.

Found at: `auras`.

Example:

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "id": "text"
    }
  ],
  "kinds": [
    {
      "id": "text"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `groups` | list of [AuraGroup](#auragroup) | no | - | - | The groups. |
| `kinds` | list of [AuraKind](#aurakind) | no | - | - | The kinds. |

### AuraGroup

A group of auras by when they apply, one switch of the Auras dialog.

Found at: `auras.groups[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | - | - | The id. |
| `default` | boolean | no | - | - | true: on by default. |
| `label` | string | no | - | - | The label. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The text. |

### AuraKind

A kind of aura with its colour and label.

Found at: `auras.kinds[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | - | - | The id. |
| `colour` | string | no | - | - | The colour name. |
| `default` | boolean | no | - | - | true: shown by default. |
| `label` | string | no | - | - | The label. |
| `rgb` | string | no | - | - | The colour as RRGGBB. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The legend sentence. |

### Company

A Battle Company: its starting force, reinforcement and special charts, advancements, hero upgrades, own units and gear, and the rules that are its own.

Found at: `companies[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "text",
  "alignment": "good"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of the company; the key every chart, advancement and campaign refers to. |
| `alignment` | string | yes | - | `good`, `evil` | good or evil. |
| `advancements` | list of [Advancement](#advancement) | no | - | - | The promotions of the company's units. |
| `aka` | list of string | no | - | - | Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused. |
| `breakPoint` | Share | no | - | - | This company's own Break Point (Muster of Isengard: "33/50", 66 percent); a whole percent, as a fraction or a percent number; default campaign.breakPoint.default. |
| `description` | string | no | - | - | The text at the head of the company's page. |
| `elvenWeaponry` | [Who](#who) | no | - | - | The models of the company that may also buy and wear Elven-made weaponry, which is otherwise restricted to Elf models. An empty object means every model. A company's own unique wargear keeps its own who. |
| `epigraph` | [Epigraph](#epigraph) | no | - | - | The quote and flavour sentence that head the company's rules. |
| `exchanges` | list of [Exchange](#exchange) | no | - | - | Rules swapped for other rules. |
| `extends` | string | no | - | - | A company of this file whose fields this one inherits where it does not write them (Elite Arnor extends Arnor). A list or object you write replaces the base's as a whole. name, faction, description, epigraph, notes and specialRules are never inherited. |
| `faction` | string | no | - | - | The faction keyword of the company; default the name. |
| `gear` | list of [Gear](#gear) | no | - | - | The unique wargear of this company. |
| `granted` | list of [Granted](#granted) | no | - | - | Special rules the company gives for free. |
| `heroUpgrades` | list of [HeroUpgrade](#heroupgrade) | no | - | - | The Company Hero Upgrades: rules a hero may take instead of a rolled result. |
| `heroes` | [Heroes](#heroes) | no | - | - | Who may be a starting hero; recruits that join as heroes. |
| `id` | string | no | - | - | A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes. |
| `label` | string | no | - | - | How the pages spell the name when the key is plainer (Lothlórien for Lothlorien). It must be the same name once accents, case and punctuation are folded; a different name is a different company. |
| `limits` | [CompanyLimit](#companylimit) | no | - | - | Limit exemptions, changed shares and keyword caps of this company. |
| `maxModels` | integer | no | - | 1..50 | The most models in this company; default campaign.company.maxModels. |
| `notes` | list of [CompanyNote](#companynote) | no | - | - | Notes of the company page, placed by section. |
| `oath` | [Oath](#oath) | no | - | - | The oath of the company. |
| `ownPath` | [OwnPath](#ownpath) | no | - | - | The units that are On Their Own Path. |
| `promotions` | list of [Promotion](#promotion) | no | - | - | Promotions to Hero for units of this company. |
| `recruit` | [Recruit](#recruit) | no | - | - | Recruitment exceptions. |
| `reinforcements` | [Chart](#chart) | no | - | - | The reinforcement chart. Required. |
| `rules` | list of [Rule](#rule) | no | - | - | Rule definitions local to this company. |
| `special` | [SpecialChart](#specialchart) | no | - | - | The special units chart. |
| `specialRules` | list of string | no | - | - | The sentences of the company's rules that have no typed form here; a typed object keeps its own text. |
| `start` | [Start](#start) | no | - | - | The starting force. Required. |
| `substitutions` | list of [Substitution](#substitution) | no | - | - | Models treated as other models for a rule. |
| `units` | list of [Unit](#unit) | no | - | - | Units local to this company (an alias with extends, a composite model...). A chart, an advancement or the starting force names them. |

### Advancement

Which units a unit may be promoted to.

Found at: `companies[].advancements[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "from": "text",
  "to": [
    "text"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes | - | - | The unit being promoted. |
| `to` | list of [AdvanceTo](#advanceto) | yes | - | - | The units it may become: a name, or {unit, with} when the promotion also gives wargear. |
| `with` | list of string | no | - | - | The wargear the unit must carry to be promoted. |

### Who

The one selector of "which models": every field narrows it, all that are set must hold, and an empty selector admits every model.

Found at: `companies[].elvenWeaponry`, `companies[].gear[].who`, `companies[].granted[].who`.

Example:

```json
{
  "alignment": "good",
  "except": [
    "text"
  ],
  "hero": true
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alignment` | string | no | - | `good`, `evil` | good or evil: the alignment of the company. |
| `except` | list of string | no | - | - | Exact unit names that are left out. |
| `hero` | boolean or null | no | - | - | true: heroes only; false: warriors only. |
| `keywords` | list of string | no | - | - | Any of these keywords of the model: its races, factions and unit types, or Cavalry for a model that rides. |
| `race` | list of string | no | - | - | Any of these races (Elf, Hobbit). A model whose profile is unknown is not refused. |
| `refusal` | string | no | - | - | Display only: what the armoury says to a model that is not admitted. Made from the fields when empty. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | Display only: how the page names the models. Made from the fields when empty. |
| `units` | list of string | no | - | - | Exact unit names (the name of the model or of its profile), never part of a name. |

### Epigraph

The quoted title and flavour sentence that head a company's rules. Flavour, not a rule.

Found at: `companies[].epigraph`.

Example:

```json
{
  "quote": "text",
  "text": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `quote` | string | no | - | - | The quoted line. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The flavour sentence after the quote. |

### Exchange

A rule models of the company swap for another.

Found at: `companies[].exchanges[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "remove": "text",
  "add": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `remove` | string | yes | - | not empty | The rule taken away. |
| `add` | string | yes | - | not empty | The rule given instead. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rulebook sentence. |

### Gear

An item: wargear, equipment, a creature or a wanderer. In a company's gear[] it is that company's unique wargear.

Found at: `companies[].gear[]`, `gear[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of the item. Identity is the name and nothing else: equal stats, class or price never make two items one. |
| `abilities` | [Abilities](#abilities) | no | - | - | The typed abilities the engine reads. |
| `aftermathEffect` | string | no | - | - | A consumable of the aftermath: the key of the campaign.aftermathEffects entry it activates. |
| `aka` | list of string | no | - | - | Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused. |
| `auras` | list of [Aura](#aura) | no | - | - | The rings the item draws. |
| `base` | string | no | - | - | The generic item this one is a version of. |
| `classes` | list of string | no | - | `melee`, `spear`, `two_handed`, `mount`, `bow`, `armour`, `throwing`, `shield`, `instrument`, `consumable`, `lance`, `banner`, `missile`, `crossbow`, `other` | What the item is, from the closed set; the first is the main class. Derived from type when the type says it. |
| `definition` | string | no | - | - | The item text shown on its tooltip. Default: the vanilla item's text. |
| `extends` | string | no | - | - | An item of this file whose fields this one inherits where it does not write them; a list or object you write replaces the base's. name, definition, note and tts are never inherited. |
| `gold` | [Rating](#rating) | no | - | - | The Gold cost; default the rating. |
| `grants` | list of string | no | - | - | Special rules the bearer gets. |
| `grantsForChosenWeapon` | [ChosenGrant](#chosengrant) | no | - | - | The rule granted for one chosen weapon. |
| `grantsSlots` | [Slots](#slots) | no | - | - | Slots the item adds (the Backpack: 3 small). |
| `id` | string | no | - | - | A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes. |
| `influence` | integer | no | - | 0..100 | The Influence cost. |
| `kind` | string | no | - | `wargear`, `equipment`, `creature`, `wanderer` | wargear, equipment, creature or wanderer. A new item needs one; an entry without a kind annotates a vanilla item. |
| `limit` | integer | no | - | 0..99 | The most models of the company that may carry it; 0 or absent: no limit. |
| `modifiers` | list of string | no | - | - | Item modifiers (elven, masterForged). |
| `mount` | string | no | - | - | A mount: the vanilla entry that holds its stat block, when it is not the item's own name. |
| `note` | string | no | - | - | A note for the people who read the file; the app may show it next to the entry. |
| `overrides` | boolean | no | - | - | true when this entry deliberately replaces a lower-layer entry (vanilla or the glossary) of the same name. Without it, defining a name that already exists is an error. |
| `pricedAs` | string | no | - | - | Sold at the price, size and restrictions of this item (Elven-made weaponry: its generic equivalent). |
| `profile` | any | no | - | - | Creatures and wanderers: their profile (unit type, stats, rules, companyFeature...). Free-form. |
| `ranged` | [Ranged](#ranged) | no | - | - | The missile profile of a bow, crossbow, throwing weapon or missile. |
| `rating` | [Rating](#rating) | no | - | - | The rating: one number, or {warrior, hero}. |
| `related` | list of string | no | - | - | Related but distinct items (Elf Bow and Longbow share a profile). |
| `requiresMount` | boolean | no | - | - | true: only a mounted model can use it (Lance, Barding). |
| `size` | string | no | - | `small`, `large` | small or large: the slot an equipment item takes. |
| `statChanges` | list of [StatChange](#statchange) | no | - | - | Characteristics the item changes. With a condition it is only a note. |
| `tts` | [GearTTS](#geartts) | no | - | - | The Tabletop Simulator figure of a wanderer, creature or fighting mount. |
| `type` | string | no | - | - | The vanilla type, from which the classes are derived (mount, bow, armour, shield, banner, spear...). |
| `unsold` | boolean | no | - | - | true: defined for its classes and text, but no armoury sells it. |
| `who` | [Who](#who) | no | - | - | Who may buy it. On a company's unique wargear: the models that may take it. |

### Abilities

The two item abilities the engine reads; every other ability is item text only.

Found at: `companies[].gear[].abilities`.

Example:

```json
{
  "attacksBonus": {
    "value": -10
  },
  "defenceBonus": {
    "value": -10
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attacksBonus` | [AttacksBonus](#attacksbonus) | no | - | - | A situational Attacks bonus. |
| `defenceBonus` | [DefenceBonus](#defencebonus) | no | - | - | A Defence bonus (shields). |

### AttacksBonus

A bonus to Attacks that holds only in a game situation; item text, never added to the profile.

Found at: `companies[].gear[].abilities.attacksBonus`.

Example:

```json
{
  "value": -10
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | integer | yes | - | -10..10 | The bonus. |
| `condition` | string | no | - | - | The condition in words. |

### DefenceBonus

The Defence a shield adds and what cancels it.

Found at: `companies[].gear[].abilities.defenceBonus`.

Example:

```json
{
  "value": -10
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | integer | yes | - | -10..10 | The bonus. |
| `against` | string | no | - | - | The attacks it counts against. |
| `cancelledByClasses` | list of string | no | - | `melee`, `spear`, `two_handed`, `mount`, `bow`, `armour`, `throwing`, `shield`, `instrument`, `consumable`, `lance`, `banner`, `missile`, `crossbow`, `other` | Classes of item that cancel it (bow, crossbow, two_handed). |
| `cancelledByItems` | list of string | no | - | - | Named items that cancel it. |
| `cancelledByTwoHandedUse` | boolean | no | - | - | true: cancelled by a hand-and-a-half weapon used two-handed (decided per fight, only shown). |
| `condition` | string | no | - | - | The condition in words. |
| `conditional` | boolean | no | - | - | true: situational, so a note on the item that the Defence never includes. |
| `liftedByRules` | list of [DefenceLift](#defencelift) | no | - | - | Rules that lift a cancellation. |
| `notWhileEngaged` | boolean | no | - | - | true: not while Engaged. |

### DefenceLift

A rule that lifts a cancellation of a Defence bonus.

Found at: `companies[].gear[].abilities.defenceBonus.liftedByRules[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "rule": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rule` | string | yes | - | - | The rule. |
| `cancels` | list of string | no | - | - | The cancelling items it lifts. |
| `whileMounted` | boolean | no | - | - | true: only while mounted. |

### Aura

A ring of influence around the bearer, on a rule, an item or a magical power.

Found at: `companies[].gear[].auras[]`, `companies[].rules[].auras[]`, `magic.powers.<name>.auras[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "radius": 1,
  "kind": "banner",
  "affects": "friendly",
  "when": "always"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | integer | yes | - | 1..48 | Inches from the edge of the bearer's base. |
| `kind` | string | yes | - | `banner`, `command`, `support`, `enemy`, `utility` | banner, command, support, enemy or utility. |
| `affects` | string | yes | - | `friendly`, `enemy`, `any`, `self` | friendly, enemy, any or self. |
| `when` | string | yes | - | `always`, `declared`, `conditional`, `target`, `cast` | always, declared, conditional, target or cast. |
| `bearer` | string | no | - | `Hero` | Hero: only a Hero bearer gets the ring. |
| `concept` | string | no | - | - | A glossary or rule name that resolves, for the chip's popup. |
| `from` | string | no | - | `rule`, `heroicAction`, `hero`, `power` | On a rule: what draws it. rule (default), heroicAction, hero or power. |
| `group` | string | no | - | - | The Auras dialog switch (an id of auras.groups); default: when. |
| `items` | list of string | no | - | - | On an item: other items that draw the same ring. |
| `keywords` | list of string | no | - | - | A filter on the affected models (tooltip only). |
| `label` | string | no | - | - | The name of this ring when it is not the owner's. The rings of one owner need different labels. |
| `los` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the ring needs line of sight (tooltip only). |
| `mergeLabels` | list of string | no | - | - | Other labels shown as this ring. |
| `replaces` | list of string | no | - | - | Labels of the rings this one supersedes. |
| `tip` | string | no | - | - | One sentence shown with the entry. |
