|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `noStartGain` | list of string | no | - | - | Starting units that keep their own Might, Will and Fate when made heroes. |
| `recruitAsHero` | [HeroGain](#herogain) | no | - | - | Every recruit joins as a Hero in the Making with these gains. |
| `who` | [Who](#who) | no | - | - | The starting units that may be made heroes. Only units and except count: the starting units are chosen by name. |

### CompanyLimit

The limits of one company: exemptions, changed shares and keyword caps.

Found at: `companies[].limits`.

Example:

```json
{
  "company": [
    {
      "keyword": "text"
    }
  ],
  "exempt": [
    {
      "limits": []
    }
  ],
  "override": {}
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `company` | list of [KeywordLimit](#keywordlimit) | no | - | - | No more than a share of the company may have a keyword. |
| `exempt` | list of [Exempt](#exempt) | no | - | - | Models or items that do not count towards limits. |
| `override` | map of Share | no | - | - | A limit's own share for this company, by limit id (Osgiliath: bow "1/2"); a fraction, or a percent number converted to the exact fraction over 100. |

### KeywordLimit

Caps the share of a company that may have a keyword.

Found at: `companies[].limits.company[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "keyword": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keyword` | string | yes | - | not empty | The keyword. |
| `percent` | number | no | - | 0..100 | The most, as a percent of the company, converted to the exact fraction over 100 (Helm's Deep: 33 is 33/100). Write this or share. |
| `share` | Share | no | - | - | The most, as a share of the company: a fraction like "1/3". Write this or percent. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rulebook sentence. |

### Exempt

A unit or an item that does not count towards some limits.

Found at: `companies[].limits.exempt[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "limits": [
    "text"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limits` | list of string | yes | - | - | The ids of the limits[] it does not count towards. |
| `item` | string | no | - | - | The item exempted; this or unit. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rulebook sentence. |
| `unit` | string | no | - | - | The unit exempted; this or item. |

### CompanyNote

A note of a company page, placed by section.

Found at: `companies[].notes[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "section": "startingCompany",
  "text": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `section` | string | yes | - | `startingCompany`, `reinforcements`, `specialChart`, `advancements`, `eliteCompany` | The section of the page: startingCompany, reinforcements, specialChart, advancements or eliteCompany. |
| `text` | string | yes | - | not empty | The note. |
| `about` | list of string | no | - | - | The units it is about. |

### OwnPath

The units that are On Their Own Path.

Found at: `companies[].ownPath`, `companies[].units[].ownPath`.

Example:

```json
{
  "units": [
    "text"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `units` | list of string | yes | - | - | The units that are On Their Own Path. |
| `path` | string | no | `"On Their Own Path"` | - | The path they follow; default On Their Own Path. |

### Promotion

What happens to a unit of the company that rolls a promotion or a Hero in the Making.

Found at: `companies[].promotions[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "from": "text",
  "on": "noChange",
  "becomes": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes | - | - | The unit. |
| `on` | string | yes | - | `noChange`, `promoted`, `heroInTheMaking` | The progression result: noChange, promoted or heroInTheMaking. |
| `becomes` | string | yes | - | - | The unit it becomes. |
| `forgo` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the player may keep the unit as it is. |
| `pathChoice` | string | no | - | - | Who chooses its path. |
| `statGain` | boolean | no | - | - | true: it also gains the Might, Will and Fate of a new hero. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The rulebook sentence. |

### Recruit

The recruitment exceptions of a company.

Found at: `companies[].recruit`.

Example:

```json
{
  "balance": [
    {
      "keyword": "text",
      "notMoreThan": "text"
    }
  ],
  "fallback": [
    {
      "unit": "text",
      "when": "wouldExceedMaxModels"
    }
  ],
  "replace": [
    {
      "alternative": "text",
      "chart": "reinforcements",
      "cost": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `balance` | list of [Balance](#balance) | no | - | - | Keyword balances. |
| `fallback` | list of [Fallback](#fallback) | no | - | - | A recruit that would break a limit takes another result. |
| `replace` | list of [Replace](#replace) | no | - | - | Swapped recruits. |

### Balance

Says one keyword may not outnumber another in the company.

Found at: `companies[].recruit.balance[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "keyword": "text",
  "notMoreThan": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keyword` | string | yes | - | not empty | The keyword that is limited. |
| `notMoreThan` | string | yes | - | not empty | The keyword it may not outnumber. |
| `onExceed` | string | no | - | - | What happens on exceeding it. |

### Fallback

Lets a recruit that would break a limit take another result.

Found at: `companies[].recruit.fallback[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "unit": "text",
  "when": "wouldExceedMaxModels"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | string | yes | - | not empty | The unit the exception is for. |
| `when` | string | yes | - | `wouldExceedMaxModels`, `memberMissing` | wouldExceedMaxModels or memberMissing. |
| `anyRoll` | boolean | no | - | - | true: any roll may be taken. |
| `charts` | list of string | no | - | `reinforcements`, `specialChart` | The charts the replacement result is taken from: reinforcements, specialChart. |
| `choose` | string | no | - | - | The words of the exception. |
| `cost` | integer | no | - | 0..100 | Influence cost. |
| `swapRollOn` | string | no | - | `reinforcements`, `specialChart` | The chart whose roll is swapped. |

### Replace

A recruit that may be swapped: a unit that takes an officer's place once the company's one is slain, or an alternative offered on some rolls of a chart.

Found at: `companies[].recruit.replace[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "alternative": "text",
  "chart": "reinforcements",
  "cost": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alternative` | string | no | - | - | For an alternative: the unit offered at no cost instead. |
| `chart` | string | no | - | `reinforcements`, `specialChart` | For an alternative: the chart (reinforcements, specialChart). |
| `cost` | integer | no | - | 0..100 | Influence cost. |
| `max` | integer | no | - | 1..50 | At most this many. |
| `playerChoice` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the player chooses. |
| `roles` | list of string | no | - | `leader`, `sergeant` | The officer roles it may take: leader, sergeant. |
| `roll` | [Roll](#roll) | no | - | - | For an alternative: the roll of that chart it replaces. |
| `unit` | string | no | - | - | The unit that takes the place (Shire: the Ranger of the North). |
| `when` | string | no | - | - | When the swap is offered. |

### Chart

The reinforcement chart: the Influence a reinforcement costs and the rows by roll.

Found at: `companies[].reinforcements`.

Example:

```json
{
  "rows": [
    {
      "roll": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` | list of [ChartRow](#chartrow) | yes | - | - | The rows; together they cover the recruiting die exactly once. |
| `influence` | integer | no | - | 0..100 | The Influence one reinforcement costs. |

### ChartRow

One row of a reinforcement or special chart. A row is exactly one of: a unit, nothing, special, choose or options.

Found at: `companies[].reinforcements.rows[]`, `companies[].special.rows[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "roll": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roll` | [Roll](#roll) | yes | - | - | The roll the row covers: a number, "2-3" or [2, 3]. |
| `blocks` | boolean | no | - | - | On a nothing row: it also blocks further rolls. |
| `choose` | string | no | - | - | The words of a row that lets the player take a result of the chart; needs scope. |
| `count` | integer | no | `1` | 1..50 | How many models; default 1. |
| `nothing` | boolean | no | - | - | The result is nothing. |
| `options` | list of [ChartChoice](#chartchoice) | no | - | - | The player picks one of these units. |
| `pick` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the player picks the unit's options. |
| `picks` | integer | no | - | 1..10 | On a choose row, how many results the player takes (1 to 10, default 1). |
| `rare` | integer | no | - | 0..50 | Rare N: at most N of this unit in the roster; the result is recruited as a lower one when exhausted. |
| `scope` | string | no | - | `above`, `any` | above: the units of the rows above the roll on the chart being rolled. any: the units of any row of both charts. |
| `special` | boolean | no | - | - | The roll goes on to the special chart (reinforcement chart only). |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The words of an options row. |
| `unit` | string | no | - | - | The result is this unit. |
| `with` | list of string | no | - | - | The options or wargear the recruit comes with. |

### ChartChoice

One of the units an options row lets the player pick, with the number of it the company may have.

Found at: `companies[].reinforcements.rows[].options[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "unit": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | string | yes | - | not empty | The unit. |
| `rare` | integer | no | - | 0..50 | Its own Rare N. |

### Rule

A special rule (keyword): its text, who it works against or for, the rings it draws.

Found at: `companies[].rules[]`, `rules[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of the rule. A rule that exists in vanilla needs overrides to be redefined. |
| `aka` | list of string | no | - | - | Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused. |
| `auras` | list of [Aura](#aura) | no | - | - | The rings the rule draws. |
| `bareTarget` | [Target](#target) | no | - | - | The target of the rule written without its bracket (Terror: all enemies; Terror (X): the keyword). Needs parameter and target. |
| `definition` | string | no | - | - | The rule text, copied from the rulebook. |
| `id` | string | no | - | - | A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes. |
| `label` | string | no | - | - | The name the pages show when the key is plainer. |
| `minor` | boolean | no | - | - | true: a minor special rule (the list a path may offer). |
| `note` | string | no | - | - | A note for the people who read the file; the app may show it next to the entry. |
| `overrides` | boolean | no | - | - | true when this entry deliberately replaces a lower-layer entry (vanilla or the glossary) of the same name. Without it, defining a name that already exists is an error. |
| `parameter` | [Parameter](#parameter) | no | - | - | Says the rule takes a bracketed argument. |
| `source` | string | no | - | - | Where the rule is printed. |
| `tag` | string | no | - | `Active`, `Passive` | Active or Passive. |
| `target` | [Target](#target) | no | - | - | Who it works against or for. |

### Target

Who a rule works against or for.

Found at: `companies[].rules[].bareTarget`, `companies[].rules[].target`.

Example:

```json
{
  "appliesTo": "own",
  "bearerKeywords": [
    "text"
  ],
  "keywords": [
    "text"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `appliesTo` | string | no | `"own"` | `enemy-keyword`, `enemy-any`, `friendly-keyword`, `own` | enemy-keyword, enemy-any, friendly-keyword or own (default). |
| `bearerKeywords` | list of string | no | - | - | The rule only works while the bearer has one of these keywords. |
| `keywords` | list of string | no | - | - | The keywords the rule is about. |
| `match` | string | no | `"any"` | `any`, `all` | any (default) or all of the keywords. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | In words, who it works against or for. |

### Parameter

Says a rule takes a bracketed argument, such as Hatred (X).

Found at: `companies[].rules[].parameter`.

Example:

```json
{
  "kind": "keyword"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | yes | - | `keyword`, `weapon`, `rollTarget`, `number`, `companyHero` | What the X is: keyword, weapon, rollTarget, number or companyHero. |
| `picks` | string | no | - | - | Who picks it. |

One line of the starting force.

Models of the company treat some model as another for a rule (the Leader counts as Faramir for Loyal to the Captain).

| `treatedAs` | string | yes | - | not empty | The model it is treated as. |
| `text` | string | yes | - | not empty | The rulebook sentence. |
| `rule` | string | no | - | - | The rule involved. |

### SubTarget

The model that is treated as another: a role of the company, or any hero with a rule.

Found at: `companies[].substitutions[].target`.

Example:

```json
{
  "hero": true,
  "role": "leader",
  "withRule": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` | boolean | no | - | - | true: any hero. |
| `role` | string | no | - | `leader`, `sergeant` | leader or sergeant. |
| `withRule` | string | no | - | - | Only a hero with this rule. |

### Unit

A unit entry. Three forms: an annotation of a lower-layer unit (the name of a vanilla unit plus properties, no definition), a unit built on another with extends and deltas, or a brand-new unit with a full definition and no base.

Found at: `companies[].units[]`, `units[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "addKeywords": [
    "text"
  ],
  "addRules": [
    "text"
  ],
  "aka": [
    "text"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `addKeywords` | list of string | no | - | - | Keywords added. |
| `addRules` | list of string | no | - | - | Special rules added at no cost. |
| `aka` | list of string | no | - | - | Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused. |
| `composite` | [Composite](#composite) | no | - | - | Makes the unit one model that counts as several. |
| `definition` | any | no | - | - | A brand-new unit: its text. |
| `extends` | string | no | - | - | The unit this one is built on: a vanilla unit (its profile is used), or a unit of this file (its fields are inherited where not written). Omit for an annotation or a brand-new unit. |
| `id` | string | no | - | - | A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes. |
| `includes` | list of [Included](#included) | no | - | - | The units this one is made of, with their points. |
| `models` | integer | no | - | 1..50 | How many models a recruit counts as against the company maximum. |
| `name` | string | no | - | - | The name of the unit. Default: the name in extends (an annotation). |
| `note` | string | no | - | - | The sentence the card prints to explain what the unit is. |
| `options` | any | no | - | - | A brand-new unit: what it may take, as the vanilla file writes its options: a list of {name, points} (and chooseOneKey / requireChooseOneKey for a choose-one group). |
| `overrides` | boolean | no | - | - | true when this entry deliberately replaces a lower-layer entry (vanilla or the glossary) of the same name. Without it, defining a name that already exists is an error. |
| `ownPath` | [OwnPath](#ownpath) | no | - | - | Marks the unit as On Their Own Path. |
| `points` | integer | no | - | 0..10000 | A brand-new unit: its points cost. |
| `profile` | any | no | - | - | A brand-new unit: its full profile, written the way the vanilla file writes one: the characteristics movement, fight, shoot ("-" for none), strength, defence, attack, wounds, courage, intelligence (and might, will, fate for a hero), and the lists race, unitType (both required), faction, specialRules, wargear, heroicActions, magicalPowers and baseSize. The app then treats the unit like a vanilla profile. |
| `race` | list of string | no | - | - | The race keywords of the unit, replacing those of the unit it extends (Goblin Hulk: a Gundabad Ogre that is a Goblin, no longer an Ogre). Only with extends. |
| `tts` | [UnitTTS](#unittts) | no | - | - | The Tabletop Simulator figure. |
| `types` | [TypeDelta](#typedelta) | no | - | - | Unit types added and removed. |
| `with` | list of string | no | - | - | The options of the base unit that are pre-selected (Tookish Hunter = Hobbit Archer with the Bow option). |

| `counts` | [CompositeCount](#compositecount) | no | - | - | What it counts as. |
| `onePhysicalCard` | boolean | no | - | - | true: one card for all parts. |
| `rules` | list of string | no | - | - | The special rules that explain how it plays. |

```json
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `add` | list of string | no | - | - | Unit types added. |
| `remove` | list of string | no | - | - | Unit types removed. |

### Followers

The rules of creatures or wanderers.

Found at: `creatures`, `wanderers`.

Example:

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "attachTo": [],
    "maxAtOnce": 0,
    "maxPerHero": 0
  }
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rules` | [FollowerRules](#followerrules) | yes | - | - | The counts. |

### FollowerRules

How many creatures a hero keeps, or how many wanderers a company has at once.

Found at: `creatures.rules`.

Example:

```json
{
  "attachTo": [
    "leader"
  ],
  "maxAtOnce": 0,
  "maxPerHero": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attachTo` | list of string | no | - | `leader`, `sergeant` | Creatures: the roles that may have one: leader, sergeant. |
| `maxAtOnce` | integer | no | - | 0..99 | Wanderers: the most in the company at once. |
| `maxPerHero` | integer | no | - | 0..99 | Creatures: the most per hero. |

### Limit

A company-wide limit on a class of items or a keyword (no more than a share of the company may carry it).

Found at: `limits[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "text",
  "roundUp": true
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | - | not empty | The id a company's limits refer to. |
| `roundUp` | boolean | yes | - | - | true: a fraction rounds up. |
| `classes` | list of string | no | - | `melee`, `spear`, `two_handed`, `mount`, `bow`, `armour`, `throwing`, `shield`, `instrument`, `consumable`, `lance`, `banner`, `missile`, `crossbow`, `other` | The item classes that count. |
| `label` | string | no | - | - | The words the pages use. |
| `maximumPercentage` | number | no | - | 0.01..100 | The most, as a percent of the company (0.01 to 100), converted to the exact fraction over 100 (33.33 is 3333/10000, not 1/3: write share). Write this or share. |
| `property` | string | no | - | - | What counts: all models. |
| `share` | Share | no | - | - | The most, as a share of the company: a fraction like "1/3". Write this or maximumPercentage. |
| `type` | string | no | - | `bow`, `throwingWeapon`, `keyword`, `class` | bow, throwingWeapon, keyword or class. |
| `value` | string | no | - | - | For a keyword limit, the keyword. |

### Magic

What Battle Companies says about magical powers.

Found at: `magic`.

Example:

```json
{
  "castingRule": "text",
  "floor": 1,
  "listed": [
    "text"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `castingRule` | string | no | - | - | The casting rule in words. |
| `floor` | integer | no | - | 1..6 | A casting value is never improved below this (2 is 2+); default 1. No power may be cast below it. |
| `listed` | list of string | no | - | - | Vanilla powers Battle Companies lists though nobody learns them. |
| `maxPerPower` | integer | no | - | 1..6 | Improvements of one power per hero; default 1. |
| `powers` | map of [Power](#power) | no | - | - | The powers by name: each a vanilla power the file gives a range and casting value. |

### Power

The range and casting value Battle Companies gives a vanilla power.

Found at: `magic.powers.<name>`.

Example:

```json
{
  "auras": [
    {
      "radius": 1,
      "kind": "banner",
      "affects": "friendly",
      "when": "always"
    }
  ],
  "casting": "text",
  "range": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auras` | list of [Aura](#aura) | no | - | - | The rings the power draws while in effect. |
| `casting` | string | no | - | - | The Casting Value a hero learns it at, such as 4+. |
| `range` | string | no | - | - | Inches, or self. |

### Path

A heroic path: how a hero levels up, as a table keyed by a roll.

Found at: `paths[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of the path. |
| `aka` | list of string | no | - | - | Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused. |
| `description` | string | no | - | - | A short description shown to the players. |
| `dice` | [DiceSpec](#dicespec) | no | - | - | The dice of the path table; default campaign.progression.hero.roll. The rows must cover them exactly once. |
| `extends` | string | no | - | - | A path of this file whose fields (rows, maximums...) this one inherits where it does not write them. |
| `heroicAction` | string or null | no | - | - | The name of the Heroic Action the path starts with, or null when it adds none. Its text is the rule's. |
| `id` | string | no | - | - | A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes. |
| `kind` | string | no | `"heroic"` | `heroic`, `custom`, `endOfPath` | heroic (default): offered to heroes. custom: the homebrew path an option hands out, hidden. endOfPath: no table, only rule. |
| `limit` | integer | no | - | 0..99 | The most heroes of a company that may take the path (the Sorcerer: 1). |
| `mastery` | string | no | - | - | The name of the Mastery rule. |
| `maximums` | map of [StatLimit](#statlimit) | no | - | - | The ceilings per characteristic, as {stat: {max, maxIncrease, best}}: max is the highest value the stat may reach, maxIncrease the most points level-ups may add to the profile, best the best (lowest) value of a stat where lower is better, such as 3 for Courage 3+. They apply together with the overall peak. |
| `note` | string | no | - | - | A note for the people who read the file; the app may show it next to the entry. |
| `rows` | list of [PathRow](#pathrow) | no | - | - | The table, one row per roll. |
| `rule` | string | no | - | - | The rule of an endOfPath path (At Path's End). |
| `signature` | list of string | no | - | - | The signature characteristics. |
| `spells` | list of string | no | - | - | The magical powers of the path (names). |
| `start` | [HeroGain](#herogain) | no | - | - | Might, Will and Fate a model starts on the path with, when it is not the usual hero start. |

### PathRow

The result of one roll on a path.

Found at: `paths[].rows[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "roll": 0,
  "options": [
    {
      "amount": 1,
      "anyHeroicAction": true,
      "anyMinorRule": true
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roll` | [Roll](#roll) | yes | - | - | The roll or range. |
| `options` | list of [PathOption](#pathoption) | yes | - | - | The alternatives of the result; the engine offers each. |
| `text` | string | no | - | - | The text of the row. Derived when absent; write it only when it cannot be derived. |

### PathOption

A closed alternative of a path result: exactly one of stat, rule, minorRule, heroicAction, power, castingValue, oneOf or one of the open choices anyMinorRule, anyHeroicAction and anyPower is set.

Found at: `paths[].rows[].options[]`, `paths[].rows[].options[].oneOf[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "amount": 1,
  "anyHeroicAction": true,
  "anyMinorRule": true
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer | no | - | 1..20 | By how much; default 1. |
| `anyHeroicAction` | boolean | no | - | - | A Heroic Action the hero does not have yet, its choice. |
| `anyMinorRule` | boolean | no | - | - | A minor special rule of the minor list, the hero's choice. |
| `anyPower` | boolean | no | - | - | A magical power of the path's spells the hero does not know yet, its choice. |
| `castingValue` | integer | no | - | 1..10 | Improves a casting value by this much. |
| `heroicAction` | string | no | - | - | A named Heroic Action. |
| `max` | integer | no | - | 1..10 | The highest the stat may reach through this result. |
| `maxTotal` | integer | no | - | 1..99 | The most such results a hero can take in total. |
| `minorRule` | [RuleRef](#ruleref) | no | - | - | A named minor special rule. |
| `oneOf` | list of [PathOption](#pathoption) | no | - | - | The hero picks one of these. |
| `power` | string | no | - | - | A named magical power. |
| `rollAgain` | boolean | no | - | - | The hero also takes its other result. |
| `rule` | [RuleRef](#ruleref) | no | - | - | Gives this special rule: a name, or a rule definition written here. |
| `stat` | string | no | - | `movement`, `fight`, `shoot`, `strength`, `defence`, `attack`, `wounds`, `courage`, `intelligence`, `might`, `will`, `fate` | Improves this characteristic. |

### Scenario

A scenario: its text sections, special rules and Victory Point objectives.

Found at: `scenarios[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | - | not empty | The name of the scenario; the key the selection tables list. |
| `aka` | list of string | no | - | - | Other spellings of the same name (true synonyms only). A spelling that already is a vanilla name is refused. |
| `armies` | string | no | - | - | The Armies section. |
| `description` | string | no | - | - | A short description shown to the players. |
| `endsAtLosses` | [LossShare](#lossshare) | no | - | - | The game ends once a company has lost this share of its starting models or more, never rounded: 3/4 ends it when the company is down to 25% or fewer. Casualties and models that fled a failed Courage test count; models that left the board voluntarily do not. The live match shows how many more models each company can lose before it. Leave it out when the scenario has no such end. |
| `id` | string | no | - | - | A stable id; default: the name as a slug. Write it only to keep an id when the name changes. |
| `layout` | string | no | - | - | The Layout section. |
| `objectives` | string | no | - | - | The Objectives section (how the game ends). |
| `outline` | string | no | - | - | The short lead-in some scenarios print before the description. |
| `rewards` | any | no | - | - | A list of {effect, name, text, who, condition}; effect is a key of campaign.aftermathEffects. Not typed. |
| `roles` | any | no | - | - | A list of {key, name}, such as attacker and defender. |
| `scoring` | list of [Scoring](#scoring) | no | - | - | The Victory Point objectives, one per printed bullet, in printed order. |
| `side` | string | no | `"both"` | `both`, `attacker`, `defender` | both (default), attacker or defender. |
| `specialRules` | any | no | - | - | A list of {name, definition, table?}; a table is {lookup, columns, rows[{min, max, cells}]}. Not typed. |
| `startingPositions` | string | no | - | - | The Starting Positions section. |
| `usesRules` | list of string | no | - | - | Rules applied without text of their own, shown by name. |

### Scoring

One scoring objective of a scenario: the sentences that award Victory Points.

Found at: `scenarios[].scoring[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "key": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | - | not empty | A key unique within the scenario. |
| `count` | integer | no | - | 0..99 | For each / eachTiers: how many items. |
| `instruction` | string | no | - | - | The note-down sentence of a secret objective, printed before the options in How it is scored. |
| `item` | string | no | - | - | For each / eachTiers: what is counted. |
| `kind` | string | no | - | - | tiers (the best tier reached), each (item times pointsEach up to count), eachTiers (every item scores its own best tier). |
| `nomination` | [Nomination](#nomination) | no | - | - | What the player notes down. |
| `options` | list of [ScoringOption](#scoringoption) | no | - | - | The printed sentences with their points. |
| `secret` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the rules keep it hidden until the end of the game. Informative: the players keep it themselves. |
| `side` | string | no | `"both"` | `both`, `attacker`, `defender` | both (default), attacker or defender. |

### Nomination

What a player notes down at the start for a secret objective. Informative: the players keep it themselves.

Found at: `scenarios[].scoring[].nomination`.

Example:

```json
{
  "from": "ownHeroes"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | string | yes | - | `ownHeroes`, `enemyHeroes`, `terrain` | ownHeroes, enemyHeroes or terrain. |
| `allowLeader` | string | no | - | `onlyHero` | onlyHero: the Leader may be picked only when the company has a single Hero. Heroes only. |
| `where` | string | no | - | `opponentHalf` | opponentHalf: a terrain piece wholly in the opponent's half. Terrain only. |

### ScoringOption

A tier of a scoring objective: its sentence and the Victory Points.

Found at: `scenarios[].scoring[].options[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "text": "text",
  "points": 0
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | - | - | The sentence. |
| `points` | integer | yes | - | 0..99 | Its Victory Points. |

### Vanilla

What Battle Companies says about vanilla things: which duplicate wins, what a vanilla unit lacks, which options are not sold.

Found at: `vanilla`.

Example:

```json
{
  "mounts": {},
  "options": {
    "exceptions": [],
    "notSold": [],
    "reason": "text"
  },
  "pins": [
    {
      "kind": "hero",
      "name": "text",
      "occurrence": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mounts` | map of [VanillaFill](#vanillafill) | no | - | - | Fill-ins for vanilla mounts, by name. |
| `options` | [VanillaOptions](#vanillaoptions) | no | - | - | The rules about vanilla options. |
| `pins` | list of [Pin](#pin) | no | - | - | The occurrence of a duplicated vanilla name that wins. |
| `units` | map of [VanillaFill](#vanillafill) | no | - | - | Fill-ins for vanilla units, by name. |

### VanillaFill

Fields a vanilla unit or mount lacks; applied only where the vanilla field is empty.

Found at: `vanilla.mounts.<name>`, `vanilla.units.<name>`.

Example:

```json
{
  "faction": [
    "text"
  ],
  "race": [
    "text"
  ],
  "unitType": [
    "text"
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `faction` | list of string | no | - | - | The faction words. |
| `race` | list of string | no | - | - | The race words. |
| `unitType` | list of string | no | - | - | The unit types. |

### VanillaOptions

The rules about vanilla options.

Found at: `vanilla.options`.

Example:

```json
{
  "exceptions": [
    {
      "unit": "text",
      "option": "text"
    }
  ],
  "notSold": [
    "text"
  ],
  "reason": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `exceptions` | list of [OptionException](#optionexception) | no | - | - | The few options the words would hide or that are read as another item. |
| `notSold` | list of string | no | - | - | Words: a vanilla option whose name contains one is not sold (banner, war horn, war drum). |
| `reason` | string | no | - | - | Why those words are not sold; the armoury shows it. |

### OptionException

An option the notSold words would hide, or that is read as another item.

Found at: `vanilla.options.exceptions[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "unit": "text",
  "option": "text"
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | string | yes | - | - | The unit. |
| `option` | string | yes | - | - | Its option. |
| `granted` | boolean | no | - | - | true: the model comes with it from the charts or the starting company. |
| `notSold` | boolean | no | - | - | true: no armoury sells it. |
| `ownItem` | string | no | - | - | An item of its own that no armoury sells, choosable under its own name. |
| `readAs` | string | no | - | - | Sold as this armoury item. |
| `reason` | string | no | - | - | Why it is not sold; the armoury shows it. |

### Pin

Records which occurrence of a name that vanilla defines twice is meant. Without a pin the first wins.

Found at: `vanilla.pins[]`.

Example:

```json
{
  "kind": "hero",
  "name": "text",
  "occurrence": 1
}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | yes | - | `hero`, `warrior`, `unit`, `item`, `rule`, `mount` | hero, warrior, unit, item, rule or mount. |
| `name` | string | yes | - | - | The duplicated name. |
| `occurrence` | integer | yes | - | 1..20 | Which occurrence is meant, counting from 1. |

## Value forms

These keys accept more than one shape.

### Roll

A chart roll: a whole number, a range "lo-hi" or a pair [lo, hi].

Accepted forms:

- a whole number 0..1000
- a string matching `^\s*([0-9]{1,3}|1000)\s*(-\s*([0-9]{1,3}|1000)\s*)?$`
- a list of 2 whole numbers

### DiceSpec

A dice specification [N]dM, N 1..10, M 2..100; d66 is refused.

A string matching `^([1-9]|10)?[dD]([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]|100)$`.

### Rating

A rating: one number for warrior and hero alike, or {warrior, hero}.

Accepted forms:

- a whole number 0..1000
- an object with the keys `warrior`, `hero`, all required

### RuleRef

A rule name, or a rule definition object that the loader hoists.

Accepted forms:

- a non-empty string
- an object, see [Rule](#rule)

### AdvanceTo

A promotion target: a unit name, or {unit, with} when the promotion also gives wargear.

Accepted forms:

- a non-empty string
- an object with the keys `unit`, `with` (required: `unit`)

### Scalar

A string or a number read as text (the rulebook version).

Accepted forms:

- a non-empty string
- a number
